summary: Normalization organizes database data to minimize redundancy and prevent insertion, update, and deletion anomalies using functional dependencies. It progresses through several normal forms. First Normal Form (1NF) requires all attributes to hold atomic values without repeating groups. Second Normal Form (2NF) builds on 1NF by ensuring no non-prime attribute has a partial dependency on a part of a composite primary key. Third Normal Form (3NF) requires 2NF compliance and removes transitive dependencies where a non-prime attribute depends on the key through another non-prime attribute. Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) is a stricter version of 3NF, requiring that for every functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a superkey.

key_terms.definition: The process of organizing data in a database to reduce redundancy and avoid insertion, update, and deletion anomalies.
A relationship where the value of one attribute, X, determines the value of another, Y (X -> Y).
A state where every attribute contains only atomic values and there are no repeating groups.
A state in 1NF where every non-prime attribute is fully functionally dependent on the whole primary key.
A state in 2NF where there is no transitive dependency of a non-prime attribute on the key.
A stricter version of 3NF requiring that for every functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a superkey.
The inability to add some data without also adding other unrelated data.
Data inconsistency caused by changing a fact in only some of the many rows where it is stored.
The unintended removal of facts when deleting a single row.
A condition where A -> B and B -> C, meaning C depends on A through B.
